summary: August Tholuck worked in religious studies and other fields. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1816–1819), where he held a post from circa 1820 to 1826, before serving at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1826 to 1877.
August Viktor Bergny was an Indologist and linguist who completed his Fil.kand. (circa 1886–1889) and fil.lic. (circa 1889–1898) at Uppsala University.

Indologist and linguist August Wilhelm von Schlegel studied at the University of Göttingen (1786–1791) under Heyne and Bürger, and later under Chézy and Hamilton. He held posts at the University of Jena (1795, 1798) and the University of Bonn (1818).

August Winter was an Indologist. He studied under Hermann Jacobi at the University of Bonn (circa 1889–1892) and completed his Ph.D. under Alfred Hillebrandt at the University of Breslau (circa 1892–1893).

Indologist and linguist August Zacharias Collin earned his fil.kand. and fil.dr. at Lund University, later studying under Rudolf von Roth (1874–1875). He was a Docent of chemistry at Lund University (1858) and a Lektor at Nicolaiskolan, Helsingborg (1864).

Auguste Ali Bourquin worked in Indology and religious studies, earning a Dr.théol. from the University of Paris by 1885. He held posts at Wilson College, Mumbai (1882) and the Royal College of Science, Arts and Commerce.

Indologist Auguste Barth studied at the University of Strasbourg (1852–1856) under Frédéric-Guillaume Bergmann. He taught at Collège Poincaré Saverne (circa 1856–1861) and Collège de Bouxwiller (1857), later becoming a member of the Institut de France (circa 1893–1916).
Auguste Comte was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Joffre until 1814 and subsequently attended École polytechnique from 1814 to 1816.

Auguste Desgodins, active in tibetology and linguistics, studied at the Major Seminary of Verdun (circa 1845–1849) and Séminaire de Saint-Sulpice (circa 1849–1850). In 1855, he was appointed as a missionary for the Paris Foreign Missions Society.

Auguste Wagener worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Bonn under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl and Christian Lassen (1845–1849) and at the University of Liège (circa 1846–1850), later serving as agrégé (1850) and professor (1858) at Ghent University.

Indologist Auguste-Louis-Armand Loiseleur-Deslongchamps studied at Lycée Charlemagne and was taught by Antoine-Léonard Chézy and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy in 1824. In 1832, he joined the Manuscript Department of the Bibliothèque nationale de France.

Indologist Augustus Frederic Rudolf Hoernle studied at Basel, Tübingen, and under Theodor Goldstücker. He held posts at Jay Narayan Inter College, Cathedral Mission College, Calcutta Madrasa, and Aliah University, and served as Philological Secretary of The Asiatic Society (1879–1891).

Aung San Suu Kyi, active in tibetology and other fields, studied at Lady Shri Ram College, University of Delhi, St Hugh's College, and SOAS University of London. She held a post at the United Nations from circa 1969 to 1971.

Indologist and linguist Aurel Mayr studied at Eötvös Loránd University, Berlin under Albrecht Weber, and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth (Ph.D. 1870–1871). From 1873 to 1905, he was professor of Sanskrit and IE linguistics at Eötvös Loránd University.
Indologist Aureliano Julio Berriz do Seixo earned a Dr. of Civil and Canonic Law at Complutense University of Madrid, where he later served as Assistant Professor of Sanskrit.

Awadh Kishore Narain was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and under Arthur Llewellyn Basham at SOAS, later serving in professorships at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1971–1987).

Linguist and Indologist Axel Erdmann studied at Uppsala University and the University of Bonn under Johann Gildemeister. He held posts at Uppsala University as Docent in Old English (1871), professor of modern European linguistics (1873–1891), and Professor of English (1904).

Axel Klein, specializing in Japanology, studied at the University of Bonn (1987–1994). He worked at Bonn (1998–2007) and the German Institute for Japanese Studies (2007–2011), before taking a professorship at the University of Duisburg-Essen in 2012.

Indologist Axel Michaels studied under Laxmi Nath Srestha, earned degrees at Hamburg and Kiel, and directed the Nepal Research Centre. He held professorships at the University of Bern (1992–1996) and Heidelberg University (starting 1996), where he also was director (1999–2002).
Ayako Nakamura works in Buddhist studies and tibetology. She earned a PhD at the University of Hamburg (attested 2009), where she also served as a Research Fellow (attested 2026).
